analyst.summary: Great Eastern Shipping just delivered its best quarterly profit ever, but a meaningful part of that came from one-time vessel-sale and foreign-exchange gains layered on top of a genuine but geopolitically-driven spike in tanker freight rates (tied to disruption near the Strait of Hormuz) - not a new sustainable earnings level. The company's underlying revenue base has actually been shrinking over the past three years, which is the more honest picture of a business that is fundamentally cyclical. The balance sheet is excellent (a large net cash position), which is a real strength through the next downcycle, but we would not read the currently very cheap valuation as a bargain being missed - it looks like the market correctly pricing a cyclical peak.
